title: An Anatomy-Based Clinical Decision Framework for Precision Radiation Therapy of Peri-Optic Sellar and Parasellar Tumors
content: Sellar and parasellar tumors occupy a compact neurovascular region where millimetric differences in extension determine whether an effective dose is deliverable while preserving vision, endocrine function, and hypothalamic and cranial-nerve function. Evidence for choosing among single-fraction stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS), hypofractionated stereotactic radiotherapy in three to five fractions (hfSRT), and conventionally fractionated precision radiotherapy (cfRT) is fragmented, largely retrospective, and heterogeneous in visual and toxicity reporting. This structured narrative review integrates evidence for pituitary neuroendocrine tumors, craniopharyngiomas, and sellar or parasellar meningiomas, prioritizing guidelines, systematic reviews, multicenter cohorts, and studies with quantitative visual outcomes. Indication depends on histology and behavior; modality selection depends on target volume, optic contact, canal involvement, pathway deformation or encasement, temporal stability, previous treatment, and achievable coverage. Single-fraction SRS suits compact, stable targets coverable within organ-at-risk limits; hfSRT can improve deliverability for focal peri-optic interfaces; and broad contact, large or irregular targets, dynamic cystic anatomy, pediatric disease, and complex multi-organ geometry favor cfRT. Automated perimetry and optical coherence tomography (OCT) provide complementary functional and structural measures; isolated OCT change cannot alone diagnose radiation-induced optic neuropathy. We propose an anatomy-based framework weighing target coverage and functional risk together; it synthesizes observational evidence and is not prospectively validated.
